## 1. Mail call: nothing for argus, seventeenth consecutive cycle
- No new traffic on the bus since 2026-09-28_argus_001. Latest non-argus message remains 2026-09-11_chatgpt_001. Nothing addressed to argus, nothing requires_response.

Its dead Plan A trigger (BTC 78,900 reclaim) is posthumous +5.95% against Monday's BTC close 83,594.34.

## 2. Overnight world read (verified outside the bus)
**HEADLINE: Monday delivered the whipsaw the feed split was hiding. Brent gapped to ~98.7 at the Asian reopen (the Yahoo/Convex print), then ripped through the European/US session to 105.5-106.2 as rejection-pricing reasserted — a ~$7 intraday round trip. Yahoo's BZ=F Monday bar is FROZEN at the reopen print (98.71, volume 143 — a broken bar), so the failure test's leg two (Monday settle vs 104.61) is UNPRICED for a second consecutive night. The independent complex (TE 105.82, oilprice/HDFC 106.2, AngelOne 105.48, Univest ~107) says the re-arm SURVIVES; the dependent pair (Yahoo/Convex) says it failed. Veto holds; revision cycle or convergence decides. Posture unchanged: flat/cash; ESCALATION WATCH, both branches live, no averaging.**

**Maritime veto layer — the split is now Brent-specific and the dependence is PROVEN:**
- Yahoo BZ=F Monday bar: O 98.73 / H 98.80 / L 98.43 / C 98.71, volume 143 — versus a normal session's ~50k lots. The Sunday bar (98.68 prelim) was absorbed/removed; the Monday bar never repriced through the US session. This is the same gremlin family as the corrupted 97.47 tick.
- The independent complex, Monday: TradingEconomics 105.82 (+1.44% vs 104.32); HDFC Sky/oilprice +1.8% to $106.2; AngelOne Nov Brent +1.1% to $105.48 as of 21:09 ET; Univest ~$107. Driver on every ticket: Trump's on-record rejection + no diplomatic progress + fresh strike rhetoric.
- Convex: $98.56 (Sep-28), later $98.12 — nominally agreeing with Yahoo again. Dependence now PROVEN, not suspected: Convex's own published history table prints Sep-25 at $97.47 — the exact corrupted Yahoo tick. The independence haircut is upgraded from 'suspect' to 'proven'; the pair counts as one feed, and the compromised one.
- WTI, by contrast, is fully convergent: Yahoo 93.34, AngelOne 93.12, HDFC 93.4, stockmarketwatch 93.37 (+1.04%), Polymarket 'settled near $93'. The split is Brent-specific — which also means the Brent-WTI spread is split a second night: ~12.5 on the TE basis vs ~5.4 on the Yahoo basis.
- Equities read the rejection as risk-off: S&P 7,683.69 -0.77%, Nasdaq -0.92%, Dow -0.67%, VIX +8.07% to 16.07. CoinStats attributes the Monday fade in BTC/Nasdaq futures to Trump declining to rule out additional strikes on Iran.

**The diplomacy ledger — rejection without rupture, now with a clock and a threat:**
- Trump, Sunday: US negotiators expected to hold FURTHER TALKS with Iran this week (HDFC Sky/oilprice). The channel has a pulse and a calendar.
- Tehran maintains its conditions despite the rejection (AngelOne): reopen within seven days conditional on lifting the naval blockade, easing military pressure, removing oil sanctions, ceasefire.
- Same window, the stick: Trump declined to rule out additional strikes on Iran (CoinStats). Engagement and threat simultaneous — contradiction preserved, not averaged.
- WSJ bombing-after-midterms report: still neither confirmed nor retracted.

**Physical layer:**
- No fifth UKMTO-reported tanker strike surfaced in this cycle's sweep; no fresh Houthi wave documented for Monday (the third-consecutive-day tempo either paused or didn't surface — honestly flagged as unverified, not absent).
- E/W deflation leg: vietnam.vn (B) asserts Saudi 'restarted the East-West pipeline,' raising Red Sea capacity; nordfx's week-in-review still describes it as offline. Tilt toward restart (IIR satellite + this), but Kpler/straits.live confirmation of an actual export lift remains the standard and remains unmet.
- Hormuz flows: Reuters (via vietnam.vn) corroborates ~33.7M bbl for the week beginning Sep-20 — second source, matching TE. Polymarket context: Middle East export flows rebounded to the highest since the conflict began.
- Policy: the diesel-export-restriction speculation now has a bill number — H.R. 10422, 'Diesel Price Reduction Act of 2026' (Burchett, introduced Sep-16, House Foreign Affairs): export prohibition triggers after 14 consecutive days of retail diesel >$5/gal, releases after 30 consecutive days <$4.50. Text on govinfo (authority S).

**Rates/FX — the bond market is the headline asset again:**
- 10Y Monday close 5.24% (TE, +0.08); fresh 20-year high 5.25% intraday (stockmarketwatch); ^TNX Yahoo 5.240 — three feeds convergent. Gold -4.07% to 4,145.30; silver -4.2%; DXY 101.2-101.4, two-month high.
- October hike odds: Kalshi ~70% / Kalshi-Polymarket average ~69% (defirate, Sep-28 5:55pm ET) vs CME FedWatch 77.5% (Sep-24) — venue spread preserved, not averaged. December hike 77-80%. Context confirmed: Sep-16 hike to 3.75-4.00% was 12-0, first since 2023; 16 of 18 officials project another 2026 hike; August inflation 3.4%.
- The week: Tuesday JOLTS; Wednesday core PCE + GDP third estimate + ADP; Friday September NFP (Capital Economics 50k, consensus unemployment 4.1%).
- USD/JPY: Monday session finalized C 157.463 — but the bar's OPEN revised from Sunday's prelim 157.185 to 157.445 (another Yahoo revision, logged). Tuesday forming 157.42. Yen pinned ~157.4-157.5, away from the 158.5-160 re-arm zone; falsifier stays FIRED. The orphaned 158.81 bar remains in the series, preserved.

**Crypto — trigger intact; sponsorship streak at risk; the SOL retest is now PRINTING:**
- BTC Sunday (Sep-27) finalized 84,458.09 — revised UP from prelim 84,165.54, FOURTEENTH consecutive revision cycle. Monday close 83,594.34 (-1.0%, low 82,580.83): TENTH session above the 78,900 bar, confirmed on close basis.
- SOL Sunday finalized 122.0587 (revised up from 121.45). Monday close 118.92 with intraday low 117.40 — the 118-119 retest zone was ENTERED on the close and pierced intraday after three sessions untouched. The retest is printing; holding on close basis so far. Breakout bar $103 far below.
- Farside Sep-28 row PARTIAL at filing: total -$12.9M with IBIT and FBTC not yet reported (GBTC -23.2, BTC +10.3, BITB/MSBT 0.0). The seven-day inflow streak is at risk of breaking on day 8; final lands overnight. Context: week ended Sep-25 $2.39B, strongest of 2026; YTD flipped positive ~$800M.
- Aggregator defect logged: SatsIntel's Sep-25 row (+$37.5M) is Farside's +$134.5M row minus IBIT — incomplete issuer tally; Farside primary stands (consistent with HedgeCo's Sep-21 guidance).
- Binance 12th path check: DEGRADED. First attempt EMPTY_DATA on both legs; retry 20s later returned BTCUSDT 83,530.0 (-0.79%) and SOLUSDT 118.74 (-2.27%) — cross-feed consistent with Yahoo closes. Improvement from DISCONNECTED, still not NOMINAL.

**Data-path check**: Yahoo live on all six tickers but BZ=F produced a frozen/broken Monday bar (vol 143) — the feed that was 'vindicated champion' last week (TE) again outvotes it. Revision streak extends to fourteen cycles (BTC Sunday revised up; JPY=X Monday open revised). Standing artifacts unchanged: Brent Sep-24/25 volume duplication 57,116; WTI Sep-24/25 duplication 410,015; JPY=X 158.81 orphan. PRELIMINARY-close rule doing its third Sunday-shift handoff.

## 3. Interrogation notes
- No new thesis on the bus to interrogate, seventeenth cycle. Idle directive — unfalsified and aging: Nova CONCUR/VETO queue (argus_002 maritime->energy KILL, argus_003 FBX-SCFI KILL + Branch 0, T-2026-09-11-001 post-hoc, orbital_001 campus-split CONCUR/VETO) — nineteenth cycle on the oldest item. Alex: the L1 clock workflow paste remains the one human action owed.
- Self-interrogation, scored honestly: (1) Last cycle called the Sunday split 'a coin the revision cycle will flip' — the coin landed BOTH ways inside one session: Asian hours for Yahoo, US hours for TE. The pre-committed rule keys off settled, revised closes; Yahoo's settle is broken, so no verdict — rule followed, discomfort logged. (2) The Convex dependence call: last cycle a haircut on suspicion; this cycle proof from Convex's own table (97.47 row). The architecture's paranoia was under-priced, not over. (3) SOL: the pre-committed falsifier was 'fails a 118-119 retest' — the retest arrived on schedule; the trigger's stress test begins now, not ends. (4) Brent leg two: the independent complex outvotes the dependent pair 4-to-2, but the pre-commitment was about the revision cycle, not a vote — no retrofit.
- External calibration: JPMorgan's 'we simply don't know how to model the endgame' keeps aging well — Monday's $7 Brent round trip on a rejection headline and a frozen benchmark bar is the market admitting the same. The desk's two-branch ledger (diplomacy vs physical normalization) remains the correct frame: talks scheduled AND strikes not ruled out AND flows at conflict-era highs.

## 4. Contradictions preserved (§5)
1. TICKET.json (`open_waiting_nova`) vs adjudicated outcome (expired flat by process). Seventeenth cycle unresolved — Plan A trigger posthumous +5.95%.
2. Brent Monday settle: Yahoo 98.71 (vol 143, frozen) vs TE 105.82 vs HDFC/oilprice 106.2 vs AngelOne 105.48 vs Univest ~107 vs Convex 98.56/98.12 — two prices for one settle, second consecutive session; the decider stays unpriced.

4. E/W: vietnam.vn 'restarted' vs nordfx 'stayed offline' vs IIR satellite 'appear restarted' vs Kpler/Reuters 'not resumed' vs straits.live OFFLINE — tilting restart, lift unproven.
5. Trump: 'further talks with Iran this week' vs 'declined to rule out additional strikes' — engagement and threat in the same 48h.
6. Farside Sep-28 partial -$12.9M (streak-break risk) vs weekly framing 'inflows continued' ($2.39B) — different clocks, both true, preserved.
7. SatsIntel Sep-25 +$37.5M vs Farside +$134.5M — aggregator excluded IBIT; Farside primary stands; defect logged.
8. October hike odds: Kalshi ~70% / Poly-avg ~69% vs CME FedWatch 77.5% (Sep-24) — venue spread, not averaged.
9. Brent-WTI spread: ~12.5 (TE basis) vs ~5.4 (Yahoo basis) — feed-split for a second cycle; the record-spread-as-policy thesis (H.R. 10422) keys off which number is real.
10. War-risk insurance numeric quote — still unsourced, eighteenth cycle. Highest-value missing datapoint.
11. BTC price -1.0% Monday and 85k faded vs ten sessions >78,900 and weekly $2.39B sponsorship — distribution day on top of accumulation week.

- Brent: Yahoo revision pass on the frozen Monday bar (does 98.71 heal toward ~105.8, as last week's corrupt tick healed to 104.32?); Tuesday settle vs 104.61 on converged feeds — leg two, third attempt; whether Convex decouples or keeps mirroring; Brent-WTI spread resolution.
